## Custom themes and color palettes

The book ships three ggplot2 theme helpers and several named color
palettes in `preamble-themes.R`. Each chapter sources this file at the
top so the functions are available throughout.

### Theme functions

| Function | What it does | Use when… |
|---|---|---|
| `theme_ct_vertical()` | Removes the y-axis line, y-axis tick marks and x-axis tick marks. Sets axis titles to bold Poppins. | Vertical / tall plots (time series, vertical bars) |
| `theme_ct_horizontal()` | Removes the x-axis line, x-axis tick marks and y-axis tick marks. Sets axis titles to bold Poppins. | Horizontal / wide plots (horizontal bars, side-by-side comparisons) |
| `theme_poppins_bold_all()` | Sets every bit of text in the plot to bold Poppins. | When you want a uniform, no-nonsense look across all elements |

Theme functions stack — call them with `+` like any other ggplot2 layer.
Later themes fill gaps left by earlier ones, so the ordering matters
only when they overlap.

### Color palettes

| Function | Colors returned |
|---|---|
| `list_ct_primary_colors()` | `primary` (#3371E7), `primary_shade1` (#00214D), `primary_shade2` (#003D9C), `primary_shade3` (#7094F5), `primary_shade4` (#C6D4FB) |
| `list_ct_secondary_colors()` | `secondary` (#F27124), `secondary_shade` (#FAAA19) |
| `list_ct_tertiary_colors()` | `tertiary` (#D8343E), `tertiary_shade` (#94343E) |
| `list_old_sha_colors()` | Legacy SHA palette — use only for backward-compat with older reports |
| `list_color_hex_codes()` | Nested list of all palettes above (flat list of named hex values) |

**Always use the variables, not hex literals.** If the brand updates its
palette, a single change to `preamble-themes.R` propagates to every
plot.

To pick one or two named colors inside a scale, slice the returned list:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(ggplot2)
source(file.path(here::here(), "preamble-themes.R"))

ggplot() +
  geom_col(aes(x = factor(1:2), y = c(15, 25),
               fill = factor(c("New Cases", "New Cases"))),
           position = "dodge") +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = list_ct_primary_colors[c("primary_shade1", "primary_shade3")]
  ) +
  theme_poppins_bold_all() +
  theme_ct_vertical()
```

## Interactive Maps

::: {.callout-tip}
## Want to go further with `leaflet`?

The data visualization chapter gets you comfortable with `mapview` for
quick looks and `leaflet` basics like `addTiles()`, `addPolygons()`,
`addMarkers()`, and `colorBin()` for choropleths. There's more under
the hood once you're ready for it — layer controls with `addLayers()`,
juggling coordinate and data bindings, and wiring maps up to Shiny for
interactivity. A deeper dive into all of that is coming soon.
:::
